title: The weak vowel schwa
what: giving every vowel its full value, so function words and unstressed syllables are never reduced ('to', 'for', 'can', 'of', the second syllable of 'problem')
summary: Advanced learners often retain full vowel sounds in unstressed syllables and function words, as this error doesn't hinder comprehension. However, it can make speech sound less natural and disrupt the rhythmic flow of English.
listenFor: Pay attention to whether you are fully articulating vowels in unstressed syllables and common function words like 'to', 'for', 'a', and 'of'.

contrasts.wrong: I need too go too the office.
contrasts.right: I need to go to the office.

contrasts.wrong: This report is fore the manager.
contrasts.right: This report is for the manager.

contrasts.wrong: A cup off coffee is essential.
contrasts.right: A cup of coffee is essential.

contrasts.note: The indefinite article 'a' reduces to schwa.

contrasts.wrong: The main prob-LEM was the budget.
contrasts.right: The main problem was the budget.
contrasts.note: The second syllable of 'problem' is unstressed and reduces to schwa.
The first syllable of 'about' is unstressed and reduces to schwa.
